transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-13
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Ross (Redwood SE), Dr. Susan Park (VantageMed), Marco Ruiz (DevOps), Linda Chen (PM), Rajiv Menon (CTO joined later)

Summary:
Brief sync to triage last week's latency regression that caused a partial SLA breach for VantageMed's patient-intake flow. Goals: align on immediate mitigations, handoff diagnostics, and plan for runbook/playbook testing. Discussed root symptom hypotheses (KV cache eviction pattern, autoscaler oscillation, routing fallback to cold model), regulatory concerns (data residency, audit logs), and next steps for an on-site joint drill.

Topics:
- Incident timeline and current state of recovery
- Hypotheses: cache eviction, autoscaler backpressure, model variant fallback
- Security & compliance impact: logs, retention, SOC2/ISO questions
- Immediate mitigations and medium-term hardenings
- Runbook handoff and on-site workshop planning

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): hi everyone thanks for joining on short notice, we know this is urgent so we'll try to be efficient. quick roll call?
[00:12] Susan (VantageMed): hey thanks, Susan here — i'm on for context and stakeholder alignment.
[00:17] Marco (VantageMed): Marco, ops — i'll be doing the access and traces.
[00:21] Linda (VantageMed): Linda product, focusing on impact to the patient intake flow.
[00:25] Maya: great. Ethan from Redwood will take the deep technical bits.
[00:29] Ethan (Redwood SE): hey all, thanks. i've pulled preliminary metrics from your telemetry that maya shared earlier.
[00:36] [00:45] Ethan: so quick synopsis — we saw a latency inflection around 2026-07-09 03:00 UTC that correlated with a spike in ephemeral cache misses and higher tokenization variance. requests routed to a fallback model variant during capacity pressure increased p95 by ~600ms, pushing you over the SLA window.
[01:05] Susan: okay yeah we noticed increased errors on the intake endpoint, but the logs are noisy. can you call out the KV cache thing? our team believes the K-V cash was fine, so i'm worried about mislabelling.
[01:22] Ethan: yeah, sometimes the auto-transcription there calls it K-V cash — but what we mean is the key-value cache for decoder KV state. we observed evictions that look like TTL churn, possibly triggered by compaction or an unseen eviction policy when GPUs were under memory pressure.
[01:38] Marco: is that from our autoscaler? we had a scale-down just before the spike.
[01:42] Ethan: exactly, the timeline shows a scale-down event ~4 minutes prior. two things likely compounding: 1) scaling decision left some in-flight requests re-routed to nodes that didn't have warm KV, 2) model fallback to a smaller quantized variant that increases token latency for some request shapes.
[02:03] Linda: the fallback — is that Redwood's routing or our policy? we thought we pinned the model.
[02:09] Maya: good q. for your live cluster you did pin the primary model, but there's a region-level fallback policy in place in case of GPU OOMs; that instantiated the quantized variant we call rdx-q4m. naming in the logs may not match your internal names — we'll send a mapping.
[02:29] [02:45] Rajiv (VantageMed, joins): hey apologies, CTO here — just joined. what's the ask?
[02:49] Maya: thanks for joining — we want to quickly align on mitigations and get permission for privileged, read-only access to some traces so Ethan can run a KV replay.
[02:58] Rajiv: yes please, we'll expedite.
[03:04] Ethan: here's what i'd propose immediate-short term: 1) temporarily disable cross-region failover while we stabilize to prevent cold-model routing, 2) increase min replicas for the worker pool for the intake route to avoid scale-down churn, 3) enable prefix caching for common prompts where feasible.
[03:22] Marco: increasing min replicas has cost impact, we have a finance window this month.
[03:25] Maya: understood — this is a tradeoff: small short-term cost for SLA compliance while we fix root cause. We'll show cost delta in the follow-up note.
[03:36] [04:00] Susan: what about security/ compliance? giving Redwood read-only access concerns our security team. we need SOC2 attestation and audit logs.
[04:09] Maya: absolutely. Redwood will provide SOC2 report and can do tenant-scoped access via your VPC/private deployment controls, plus all access will be logged and time-limited. we also support KMS-wrapped logs if necessary.
[04:24] Linda: perfect, please include the retention implications — we have patient PII redaction concerns.
[04:32] Ethan: for the replay we'll ask only for anonymized request IDs and the shape of token sequences; we can do the replay on your staging if you prefer, or Redwood can accept encrypted artifacts.
[04:47] [05:15] Ethan: quick deep dive: reproduction attempt in a sac staging cluster: when we forced a scale-down pattern and replayed the traffic, we saw the same per-shard cold-start penalty. The KV warmup cost seems non-linear with sequence length; the longer sequences suffer more because warmup requires extra KV fetch cycles.
[05:39] Marco: do you suspect any kernel-level bug — something in the runtime selection?
[05:44] Ethan: it's possible; our runtime chooses kernels and memory layout based on sequence distribution. there was a kernel switch on 2026-07-08 in the hosted pool (optimization patch) that may have changed memory pressure characteristics. we need to confirm if your cluster was on the new runtime.
[06:02] Maya: i'll check the release tagging and provide the rollout map.
[06:07] Susan: if it's a runtime change, that feels high risk. we expected no changes without customer opt-in.
[06:12] Maya: correct — the hosted rollout should be opt-in for pinned clusters; but region-level infra optimizations sometimes flow differently. we owe you the exact rollout map and apologize for the lack of clarity.
[06:24] [07:00] Ethan: mitigation roadmap (short/medium): short — raise min replicas, disable cross-region fallback, pin model variant to rdx-1b-static for intake; medium — kernel rollback or targeted patch, improved autoscaler hysteresis, and explicit KV prewarm on failover. long — runbook drills and observability tags to catch warm/cold transitions earlier.
[07:34] Linda: can you quantify cost of raising min replicas by 2 in our reported cluster?
[07:40] Maya: we'll run the numbers and include token-level unit cost delta in the follow-up.
[07:45] [08:15] Rajiv: besides cost, what about our regulatory posture — does the rollback or rollback window trigger any compliance flags?
[08:22] Ethan: no compliance flags for rollback itself; audit logs will show change. any log access will follow your KMS and retention rules. we'll include a compliance note.
[08:33] Susan: ok. also we observed higher tail errors for a specific route: POST /intake/v2/verify — that had increased 500s during the event.
[08:43] Ethan: yes that's the flow with longer sequences. during the fallback to quantized model, tokenization behavior changed slightly and some upstream validation failed causing 500s. will share example request/response pairs.
[08:58] [11:00] Maya: quick procedural question — what's your preferred channel for sharing traces? secure S3 with KMS, or a temporary VPN-exposed endpoint?
[11:08] Marco: secure S3 KMS preferred. we'll provision a role for read-only.
[11:13] Maya: great. we'll send the bucket policy template.
[11:20] Ethan: one more technical note — we recommend adding a short-term circuit breaker for the intake route to fail-open to a cached response (with a conservative TTL) rather than hitting the fallback model during bursts. this reduces tail latency while preserving correctness for common prompts.
[11:44] Linda: that sounds promising but we need product approval.
[11:47] Maya: we'll provide a PRD stub for the circuit breaker.
[11:53] [15:00] Ethan: about the kernel/ runtime patch — we can either roll back the minor optimization or deploy a micro-patch to adjust memory alloc thresholds. rollback is faster but loses perf benefits; patch keeps perf but takes extra validation. recommendation: roll back to restore SLA immediately and then reintroduce with test gating.
[15:22] Rajiv: rollback then retest in staging, yes.
[15:28] Maya: ok noted.
[15:33] [20:00] Susan: our timeline is tight — we have a compliance review on 2026-07-21 and we need the SLA restored by then.
[20:08] Maya: we'll prioritize the rollback and the replica increase as the first two items.
[20:12] Marco: i'll get the read-only role and share traces by 2026-07-14.
[20:18] Ethan: once we have traces i'll run the KV replay, capture heatmaps, and produce a recommended patch.
[20:28] Linda: can you include a short checklist for the runbook workshop so we can prepare stakeholders?
[20:34] Maya: yes, we'll circulate an agenda: incident timeline review, hands-on replay, failover drill, and action-item assignment.
[20:41] [30:00] Ethan: quick note on observability: adding a warm/cold KV tag and model-variant routing tag will let us create alerts that preempt this prior to SLA breach. we'll propose alert thresholds and pager escalation.
[30:18] Susan: good. include thresholds and estimated false positive rate.
[30:24] [40:00] Maya: recap of immediate owners — maya will send the rollout map and cost delta; ethan will reproduce and recommend patch; marco will provide traces; linda will coordinate internal approvals; rajiv will sign off on rollback if reproduction confirms.
[40:22] Rajiv: confirmed.
[40:26] [47:00] Maya: any other open questions?
[47:06] Linda: none from product.
[47:10] Marco: no.
[47:12] Ethan: nothing else technical for now.
[47:15] Susan: thanks, appreciate the quick turn.
[47:18] Maya: thanks all — we'll follow up with the artifacts and a proposed time for the on-site workshop.
[47:26] Rajiv: thanks.

End of transcript.
